Subject: Dedicated sizing: promotional burst + jitter (Halo Commerce)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for taking this — I'm Sara, Head of Infrastructure at Halo Commerce. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a Reserved GPU plan and need a quick sizing sanity check ahead of our exec sync next week. I've attached a one-week token-level sample from last month's promotional window (halo_telemetry_20240312.csv). A few highlights:

- Baseline: ~120 QPS steady (read-heavy product search/completion calls) during off-peak.
- Promo windows: 2-3 hour spikes where traffic multiplies ~6-8x, with short 20-60s microbursts inside those windows.
- Prompt mix: 70% short completions (avg 45 tokens prompt / 60 tokens response), 30% multi-turn chat-ish flows (avg 120 tokens prompt / 240 tokens response) when customers converse with assistants.
- Session behavior: 40% of requests are session-affine (we persist a KV cache per session), the rest are stateless completions.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end 300ms for baseline, willing to accept 500ms p95 during burst windows if fallback is engaged.

What we'd like from you: a back-of-envelope GPU footprint and any questions that would help you produce a more concrete Reserved capacity recommendation. Are there quick guardrails you use to translate this token/traffic mix into GPU counts and GPU types?

Attachments: halo_telemetry_20240312.csv (csv sample, 7MB)

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of Infrastructure | Halo Commerce
ops@halo-commerce.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@halo-commerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2024 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: promotional burst + jitter (Halo Commerce)

Sara — appreciate the sample and the concise summary. This is the right level of detail for an initial sizing. Two quick asks so we can give you an honest back-of-envelope: 

1) Can you confirm the breakdown of request types at the token level (the CSV helps — a small pivot showing counts by prompt-length bucket and response-length bucket is ideal).
2) What are your P50/P95 generation latency SLAs separately for short completions vs chat flows? You mentioned p95 300/500ms — is that strict p95 for user-facing requests or an internal objective?
3) Do you require private (VPC/on-prem) deployment for data residency, or is hosted Dedicated fine?
4) Any constraints on committing to a minimum GPU class (e.g., Ampere A100 vs Hopper H100) or specialized quantized variants?

I'll attach a lightweight sizing sheet we'd normally use to convert token velocity into GPU-hours and expected peak occupancy. If you can return the pivot mentioned in (1) and confirm (2)-(4), we can run a quick estimate and propose a Reserved capacity band (min/target/max) plus a fallback routing policy.

Attachment: redwood_sizing_template.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

Best,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Pre-Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: promotional burst + jitter (Halo Commerce)

Adding a quick thought from the capacity side — Marcus, Sara:

- For mixed prompt shapes like this we typically recommend planning around a composite token-rate (weighted by request type) and then sizing for 95th-percentile burst concurrency rather than average QPS. That helps avoid under-committing for the 20-60s microbursts you called out.
- If Halo can tolerate graceful degradation during the worst microbursts, consider a 2-tier Reserved plan: primary pool sized for sustained burst (4–6x baseline) + a small overflow burst pool (spot or smaller GPU class) to catch the 6–8x tail.
- KV cache locality matters. If 40% of requests are session-affine, ensure session-pin affinity to keep KV cache warm; otherwise occupancy goes up significantly.

Happy to run the numbers once the CSV pivot is back — we can also sketch a canary rollout to validate burst behavior before committing.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Pre-Sales Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Patel <sara@halo-commerce.com>

Marcus / Marissa — thanks, both. I've attached the pivot (halo_telemetry_20240312.csv) with prompt/response buckets and a short notes tab. Answers inline: 

- P50/P95 targets: user-facing p50 120ms, p95 320ms for short completions; chat flows p50 200ms, p95 420ms. Those are product targets; we can relax to ~500ms p95 during exceptional microbursts.
- Deployment: we prefer Hosted Dedicated in us-east initially, with the option to move to VPC later for the enterprise contract.
- GPU class: Halo prefers H100 if cost permits; otherwise A100 is acceptable with quantized model variants.

Would you both be available for a 30-minute sizing workshop next week? I dropped a calendar link in the Drive folder. If you can produce a quick min/target/max Reserved GPU band from what's attached, that will help our execs decide whether to proceed to commitment.
